primary_sources.title: Somatic mutant clones colonize the human esophagus with age
primary_sources.license_status: XML notice allows download for text mining consistent with UK copyright law; no CC redistribution license asserted. Raw article text excluded from public package.
primary_sources.inspection_depth: All28 main-body paragraphs inspected, including reported method summaries; detailed supplementary MethodsS1-S7, supplementary tables and raw sequencing data were not acquired.

anchors.original_measurement_interpretation: 844 contiguous normal-esophagus samples from nine organ donors; technical coverage and selected whole-genome samples are distinct units.
8,919 coding mutation calls merged spatially into6,935 putative events; source event label is not an authenticated count of de novo mutation births.
dN/dS is interpreted as relative probability of reaching detectable clone size, after mutation-context controls.
NOTCH1 prevalence can be higher in normal esophagus than in cancers; prevalence is not malignant transformation.
Multiple acquisitions and shared clone histories occur; per-biopsy genotype counts need lineage grouping.
Main text distinguishes normal-tissue signatures from cancer-associated APOBEC processes; no quantitative model transfer is inferred.
Source discusses differences between normal-clone prevalence and cancer origins; no TMD intervention follows.

primary_sources.title: Mutant clones in normal epithelium outcompete and eliminate emerging tumors
primary_sources.license_status: XML notice allows download for text mining consistent with UK copyright law; no CC redistribution license asserted. Raw article text excluded from public package.
primary_sources.inspection_depth: All71 body paragraphs inspected, including main narrative, available Methods and embedded Extended Data captions; supplementary note/tables, source data, images and videos were not acquired or replayed.

anchors.original_measurement_interpretation: Whole-tissue lesion density and growth trajectories are endpoint observations; lesions are nested within animals.
Targeted sequencing reports11,149 mutations from141 tumors across time points; neither is an independent mutation-birth denominator.
Observed clonality and selected genes vary between early and surviving lesions, consistent with survival/clonal competition.
Transgenic DN-Maml1 induction accelerates lesion loss in mice; this is an existing intervention study, not TMD or a patient treatment.
DBZ competition perturbation changes tumor loss in the source mouse model; no procedure or dosage is proposed here.
Whether analogous micro-tumor elimination occurs in humans is explicitly unknown in the source.
Patchwork visualization combines measured clone properties with simulated nesting/placement where unresolved.
dN/dS selection concerns the probability a clone reaches a detectable size, not direct measurement of mutation production.
Methods report no prespecified statistical sample-size calculation, no randomization and no investigator blinding; lesion counts are nested.
Extended Data4 gives89/64 tumors from2/9 mice for area measurements, and80/63 for other eligibility-specific summaries; do not merge these totals.
81 normal epithelial micro-biopsies came from two mice; biopsies are not81 independently randomized animals.
DN-Maml1 intervention panels report seven control and nine induced mice; dominant negative names a molecular construct, not TMD natural dominance.
Source simulation outputs are model runs with ABC-selected parameters, distinct from measured DBZ/control mice and uncertain human translation.
